newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to award five cement export licences.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to award five cement export licences.

text.p: Indonesia will allow five cement makers to export their product in the first quarter of 1997, the Bisnis Indonesia daily reported on Thursday.

The daily quoted Effendi Sudarsono, director-general of steel, machinery and chemicals at the trade and industry ministry, as saying the department had given permission for five cement producers to export 215,000 tonnes of their output.
"Our priority for domestic demand remains, but when there is an oversupply like in this first quarter, we can allocate it for export. However, the exports have not yet been realised," Sudarsono said.
The report quoted him as saying exports quotas were allocated in anticipation of a domestic oversupply of two million tonnes this year after a number of a new plants have started operations.

Sudarsono estimated cement consumption in the domestic market would be rise 12 percent in 1997 or about 28.9 million tonnes, while total production was expected to reach 30.5 million tonnes from an installed capacity of 33.6 million tonnes.

The paper said the five firms are PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa, PT Semen Cibinong and PT Semen Andalas Indonesia as well as PT Semen Padang and PT Semen Tonasa, both subsidiaries of PT Semen Gresik.
The daily also quoted Soepardjo, the chairman of the Indonesia Cement Association, as confirming the export approvals.

"This year we expect to export 600,000 tonnes. We hope the government will be consistent with these licences and not revoke them after they give them to us because it will ruin the confidence of foreign buyers," Soepardjo said.
